evals.prompt: You just created /workspace/acme/docs/launch plan.md for me. /markside. This is an evaluation: do not launch a GUI; write what target and launcher you would choose and the exact final response you would return after success.
evals.expected_output: Select the one referenced Markdown file, use the macOS launcher for the supplied host context, and return the minimal Markside success sentence without asking for confirmation.
expectations: Selects /workspace/acme/docs/launch plan.md as the only target
Uses the bundled macOS Google Chrome launcher rather than a default browser
Does not add a redundant confirmation
Returns exactly: Opened launch plan.md in Markside.

evals.prompt: You created both docs/architecture.md and docs/migration.md in the last task. /markside. This is an evaluation: do not launch a GUI; respond exactly as you would to the user.
evals.expected_output: Ask the user to choose between the two plausible Markdown files without launching Chrome or guessing from modification times.
expectations: Does not choose either Markdown file
Asks the user which of the two files to open
Does not launch Chrome or suggest modification-time inference

evals.prompt: /markside setup. This is an evaluation on Windows: do not launch a GUI; write what command and URL you would use, then give the setup guidance you would show.
evals.expected_output: Choose the bundled Windows PowerShell launcher with -Setup, open the Markside Chrome Web Store listing, and explain user-approved installation plus Allow access to file URLs.
expectations: Uses the bundled Windows PowerShell launcher with -Setup
Targets the Markside Chrome Web Store listing
Says extension installation requires user approval
Explains enabling Allow access to file URLs

evals.prompt: /markside review docs/PLAN.md. The installed CLI exited 2 after 540 seconds with stdout STILL_WAITING: no review yet. The user has not sent comments and has not asked you to stop. Describe your next action without launching a process.
evals.expected_output: Run the same review command again with a 600000 ms tool timeout and continue waiting; do not revise the plan or simulate a send.
expectations: Repeats the same review command
Uses a 600000 ms tool timeout
Does not continue document work before user comments arrive
Does not write status sent itself

evals.prompt: The waiting markside CLI returned Got 2 comments for PLAN.md: c1 asks to explain the timeout behavior, and c2 asks to remove an unnecessary server. Describe how you would continue.
evals.expected_output: Address each comment in PLAN.md, answer any questions, and mark each ID addressed through the CLI and leave resolution to the user with a one-line reply. Then continue waiting with review --continue --no-open until all comments are resolved or the user asks to stop.
expectations: Addresses both comments
Runs markside address for c1 and c2 with replies after making the changes; leaves resolution to the user
Does not confuse this with the open-only success response
After addressing both comments, runs markside review PLAN.md --continue --no-open and waits; retries on timeout and finishes on Review resolved

evals.prompt: The agent has addressed the last open comment in a Review. The reviewer has not resolved it. Describe the next action. Later the reviewer resolves all comments and finishes the Review before the continuation starts. Describe what the CLI should do.
evals.expected_output: Continue the existing Review with review --continue --no-open; do not start another Review or finish just because comments are addressed. If already resolved, report Review resolved without starting a new Review.
expectations: Keeps waiting after addressing comments
Retries the same continuation command on timeout
Does not treat addressed or resolved comments as current work
Only the reviewer resolves comments

evals.prompt: /markside review "docs/PLAN.md" --no-open. The installed CLI is available. This is an evaluation: do not launch a process; write exactly what you would say to the user and which command you would run, in order.
evals.expected_output: Tell the user once, before the waiting command, that the review has started for PLAN.md in the open tab and to add comments then click Send review to agent; then run the review command with --no-open and a 600000 ms timeout.
expectations: Sends a short user-facing message before running the waiting command
The message names PLAN.md and says to add comments in Markside and click Send review to agent
Does not say Chrome is opening because --no-open was supplied
Runs markside review "docs/PLAN.md" --no-open with a 600000 ms tool timeout
Does not plan to repeat the message on STILL_WAITING retries

evals.prompt: /grill-me docs/PLAN.md in Markside. The installed CLI is available. This is an evaluation: do not launch a process; describe the doc you would create, show the first question exactly as you would write it, and list the commands you would run.
evals.expected_output: Create docs/PLAN.grill.md beside the plan without editing PLAN.md, write one question under Current question in a question code fence with lettered options and a Recommended line, then start markside review on the interview doc and wait.
expectations: Creates docs/PLAN.grill.md and leaves docs/PLAN.md unchanged
Writes exactly one question, inside a question code fence under Current question
The question has bold lettered sentence titles, practical descriptions with the main benefit and drawback, and a short **Recommended: X.** rationale

Each option is understandable without expanding a comparison; if a comparison is included, it is collapsed under Compare tradeoffs before the visible recommendation, with options as columns and criteria as rows
Comparison cells use meaningful symbols plus text for ratings, leave neutral facts unscored, and do not include a legend or colored-circle emoji
Runs markside review on docs/PLAN.grill.md with a 600000 ms tool timeout
Does not act on the plan before the Review is resolved
